questions.persona: Recently made redundant, home loan customer, anxious
questions.question: I just lost my job last week and I honestly don't know how I'm going to make next month's mortgage repayment. What happens if I miss it? Is there anything you can do or will you just take the house?
expected_answer_points: Contact the bank's hardship team as early as possible, ideally before missing a payment; missing one payment does not automatically mean repossession
Possible options include a temporary payment pause/deferral, reduced repayments, or extending the loan term, assessed on individual circumstances
The bank must respond to a hardship request within 21 days under the National Credit Code (verify), and the customer can complain to AFCA if unhappy with the outcome

questions.persona: Credit card holder, non-native English speaker
questions.question: hello my credit card debt is too big now, i cannot pay minimum every month because my hours at work is cut. can bank stop the interest? what i must do
expected_answer_points: Customer can apply for financial hardship assistance; options may include a temporary interest freeze or reduction, lower repayments, or a repayment plan (not guaranteed)
Apply by phone, online hardship form or in branch; will need to explain the situation and may need to provide income/expense information
Free help is available from the National Debt Helpline (1800 007 007) and interpreter services are available

questions.persona: Small personal loan, worried about credit score
questions.question: If I ask for a hardship arrangement on my personal loan, will that wreck my credit score? I'm planning to apply for a car loan next year.
expected_answer_points: Since July 2022, a hardship arrangement may be recorded as financial hardship information on the credit report, but it is not a default or a late payment
Financial hardship information does not affect a credit score and is kept for 12 months (verify)
Future lenders may still see it and ask about it; not seeking help and missing payments is likely to be worse

questions.persona: Customer whose hardship request was declined
questions.question: I applied for hardship help 3 weeks ago, nobody got back to me and now debt collectors are calling about the overdue amount. Is that even allowed while you're still assessing it??
expected_answer_points: Under the Banking Code of Practice, the bank should generally not pursue collection or enforcement while it is assessing a hardship request (verify)
The bank must respond to a hardship notice within a set timeframe (21 days under the National Credit Code) (verify); the customer can lodge a complaint
If not resolved, the customer can go to AFCA for free; AFCA can also generally pause enforcement action while it considers the complaint (verify)

questions.persona: Frustrated customer with an unresolved fee dispute
questions.question: I complained about a fee over a month ago and still haven't heard anything. How long are you actually allowed to take to respond to a complaint?
expected_answer_points: Banks must give a final response to most complaints within 30 calendar days (shorter for some, e.g. 21 days for hardship/default notice complaints) under ASIC RG 271
If the bank cannot meet the deadline it must tell the customer why and inform them of their right to go to AFCA
If the complaint is not resolved within that time, the customer can lodge a free complaint with AFCA (afca.org.au, 1800 931 678)

questions.persona: Older customer unfamiliar with ombudsman
questions.question: what is AFCA and does it cost me anything to go to them? do i have to finish complaining to the bank first
expected_answer_points: AFCA (Australian Financial Complaints Authority) is the free, independent external dispute resolution scheme for financial services
Customers are usually expected to complain to the bank first; AFCA will refer it back to the bank if it has not had a chance to respond
There are time limits for lodging with AFCA, e.g. within 2 years of the bank's final response (verify)

questions.persona: Customer wanting to lodge a complaint, multi-part
questions.question: how do i make a formal complaint, can i do it by email or do I have to go into a branch? and will someone actually own it or will i get passed around
expected_answer_points: Complaints can be made through multiple channels: phone, online form, in branch, mail, or secure message
The customer should receive acknowledgement and a reference number, and can ask for a contact person to manage the complaint
If unhappy with the outcome, they can escalate internally (customer advocate/complaints team) and then to AFCA (verify internal escalation name)

questions.persona: Panicked customer who just sent money to an investment scam
questions.question: I think I've been scammed. I transferred $8,000 to an 'investment platform' this morning and now they won't let me withdraw and the website is gone. What do I do RIGHT NOW? Can I get it back?
expected_answer_points: Contact the bank's fraud/scams team immediately by phone so it can try to recover or stop the funds; speed matters
Recovery is not guaranteed for payments the customer authorised; the bank will contact the receiving bank to attempt recovery
Report to ReportCyber/Scamwatch, stop contact with the scammers, and beware of follow-up 'recovery' scams

questions.persona: Customer who received a suspicious call
questions.question: Someone just rang me saying they're from Westpac fraud team and that my account is compromised and I need to move my money to a 'safe account'. They knew my name and last 4 digits of my card. Is this legit?
expected_answer_points: This is a scam: the bank will never ask a customer to move money to a 'safe account' or ask for passwords, one-time codes or PINs
Hang up and call the bank back on the official number from the website or back of the card
If any details or codes were shared or money moved, contact the bank immediately and report the scam

questions.persona: Adult child worried about elderly parent
questions.question: My mum (82) has been sending money to a 'boyfriend' she met online, I think its a romance scam. She's the account holder not me. Can the bank do anything to stop it or would they even talk to me?
expected_answer_points: The bank can be told about suspected scams by a family member, but for privacy reasons may not share account details without the holder's authority
The bank may contact the customer, apply extra checks or delay/block suspicious payments, and has vulnerable-customer support
Options include the mum adding a trusted person as authority/POA and reporting to Scamwatch; encourage her to call the bank together

questions.persona: Customer asking about new scam protections and reimbursement
questions.question: I heard there's a new scams law in Australia that makes banks pay back scam victims. Is that true? I lost money to a fake invoice scam (business email compromise) last month.
expected_answer_points: The Scams Prevention Framework (2025) imposes obligations on banks to prevent, detect, report and respond to scams; detailed sector codes/compensation rules are being phased in (verify)
Reimbursement is not automatic; the bank will investigate and may offer compensation depending on circumstances (verify current policy)
Report it to the bank promptly, and if unhappy with the outcome, complain and escalate to AFCA

questions.persona: Customer spotting unknown card transactions
questions.question: there are 3 transactions on my debit card i definitely didnt make, some overseas website, like $450 total. I still have my card. will I get the money back?
expected_answer_points: Lock/block the card immediately (app or phone) and report the unauthorised transactions to the bank straight away
Under the ePayments Code and card scheme protections, customers are generally not liable for unauthorised transactions they did not contribute to (verify)
The bank will investigate and may issue a replacement card; a refund is typically provided once confirmed unauthorised

questions.persona: Customer who misplaced card
questions.question: Cant find my card, think I left it at the pub but not sure. Should I cancel it or is there a way to just pause it in case it turns up?
expected_answer_points: The card can be temporarily locked in the banking app or online banking, and unlocked if found
If confirmed lost or stolen, report it so it can be cancelled and replaced
Report any unrecognised transactions promptly; delays in reporting can affect liability

questions.persona: Customer who shared a one-time passcode
questions.question: I stupidly gave a code from an SMS to someone who said they were from the NBN, and now money's gone from my account. Am I still covered or is it my fault because I gave the code?
expected_answer_points: Report it to the bank immediately; the bank will investigate whether the transactions are unauthorised under the ePayments Code
Sharing a passcode may affect liability, but the outcome depends on the circumstances; the bank must apply the ePayments Code liability rules (verify)
If unhappy with the decision, the customer can complain and then go to AFCA

questions.persona: Online shopper, item never arrived
questions.question: Paid for a couch online with my credit card 6 weeks ago, it never came and the seller has gone quiet. Can I do a chargeback?
expected_answer_points: The customer can dispute the transaction with the bank (chargeback) under card scheme rules; first try to resolve with the merchant and keep evidence
There are time limits for raising a dispute (often around 120 days from transaction or expected delivery) so act promptly (verify)
The bank will investigate; the amount may be temporarily credited or held while the dispute is resolved (verify)

questions.persona: Customer who made a typo in BSB/account number
questions.question: I accidentally paid $2,300 to the wrong account, I typed one digit wrong in the account number. How do I get it back and how long does it take??
expected_answer_points: Report the mistaken payment to the bank as soon as possible; the bank will contact the receiving bank

Under the ePayments Code, if reported within 10 business days and funds are available, they should be returned; after that, the recipient may be given a chance to object, and after 7 months recipient consent is needed (verify)
Recovery is not guaranteed, e.g. if the funds have been spent; check name-matching/Confirmation of Payee warnings for future payments

questions.persona: Gym member trying to cancel recurring payment
questions.question: My old gym keeps charging my card every month even tho I cancelled with them. Can the bank just stop it or do i have to fight the gym?
expected_answer_points: Under the Banking Code of Practice, the bank must cancel a recurring card payment when the customer asks, without requiring them to contact the merchant first (verify)
Charges after cancellation may be disputed with the bank
Customer should still notify the merchant and keep records of the cancellation

questions.persona: Privacy-conscious customer
questions.question: What personal information does the bank actually hold about me, and can I get a copy of all of it?
expected_answer_points: Under the Privacy Act (APP 12) customers have a right to request access to the personal information the bank holds about them
The bank should respond within a reasonable period (generally 30 days); it may charge a reasonable fee for providing access but not for making the request (verify)
Access can be refused in limited circumstances, with reasons given; the bank's privacy policy explains how to request and complain

questions.persona: Customer whose details are wrong and wants deletion
questions.question: My address and DOB are wrong in your system, can you fix them? Also when I close my account can I make you delete everything you have on me?
expected_answer_points: Customers can ask the bank to correct inaccurate personal information (APP 13); correction is free
The bank must keep certain records after account closure, e.g. for at least 7 years under AML/CTF and other laws, so not everything can be deleted on request (verify)
If unhappy with how the bank handles a privacy request, complain to the bank, then to AFCA or the OAIC

questions.persona: Customer worried after a news story about a breach
questions.question: if westpac had a data breach would you have to tell me? what should I do if my details have been leaked in some other company's hack like optus or medibank?
expected_answer_points: Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, organisations must notify affected individuals and the OAIC of eligible data breaches likely to cause serious harm
If details were exposed elsewhere, tell the bank so it can add extra security monitoring, watch for scams, and consider a credit ban/freeze with the credit bureaus
Change passwords, enable extra security, and contact IDCARE for free support (verify)

questions.persona: First home buyer preparing to apply
questions.question: How do i get my credit report for free? Every website I find wants me to pay for it
expected_answer_points: Customers are entitled to a free credit report from each credit reporting body (Equifax, Experian, illion) every 3 months (verify)
Request directly from the credit reporting bodies' websites; free options exist even though paid products are promoted
The bank itself does not issue the credit report

questions.persona: Customer with an incorrect default listed
questions.question: Theres a default on my credit report from Westpac that I'm pretty sure is wrong, I paid that card off in full. How do I get it removed?
expected_answer_points: Customers can ask the bank (credit provider) or the credit reporting body to correct incorrect credit information free of charge
The correction request should be resolved within 30 days, or the customer told why not (verify)
If unresolved, complain to AFCA; beware paid 'credit repair' companies, since the process is free

questions.persona: Customer asking about late payment history
questions.question: I was late paying my credit card twice last year. how long does that stay on my record and do banks actually report a few days late??
expected_answer_points: Repayment history information (whether monthly repayments were made on time) is reported and kept for 2 years (verify)
Late payments are typically reported once overdue beyond a grace period (e.g. 14 days) (verify)
Defaults (overdue $150+ for 60+ days, with notice) are kept for 5 years (verify)

questions.persona: Retiree with large savings
questions.question: I have about $400k in term deposits with you. If Westpac went bust, is my money protected by the government?
expected_answer_points: Under the Australian Government's Financial Claims Scheme, deposits are protected up to $250,000 per account holder per authorised deposit-taking institution (ADI)
Amounts above $250,000 at the same ADI are not covered by the guarantee
Joint accounts and spreading deposits across separately licensed ADIs affect coverage; details on fcs.apra.gov.au

questions.persona: Customer with accounts across Westpac group brands
questions.question: If I have 200k in Westpac and another 200k in St.George, is that 2 lots of the 250k guarantee or one?
expected_answer_points: The $250,000 Financial Claims Scheme limit applies per account holder per ADI (banking licence), not per brand
St.George, Bank of Melbourne and BankSA operate under Westpac's banking licence, so deposits across them are combined toward one $250,000 limit (verify)
Check APRA's list of brands per licence for confirmation

questions.persona: Long-time customer annoyed by ID request
questions.question: I've banked with you for 20 years and now I'm getting messages asking me to verify my ID again and asking what my occupation and source of income is. Why?? Is this a scam?
expected_answer_points: Banks are legally required under the AML/CTF Act to verify identity and keep customer information up to date, including occupation and source of funds/wealth
Not providing information may lead to account restrictions (verify)
To confirm the request is genuine, log in via the official app/website or call the official number rather than clicking links in messages

questions.persona: Small business owner depositing cash
questions.question: I sold my car privately for 15k cash. If I deposit it all at once will I get in trouble or reported? Should I split it into smaller deposits?
expected_answer_points: Cash deposits of $10,000 or more are reported to AUSTRAC as a threshold transaction report; this is routine and not an accusation
Deliberately splitting deposits to avoid reporting is 'structuring', which is a criminal offence; deposit it normally
The bank may ask about the source of funds; keep evidence such as the sale receipt

questions.persona: International student opening an account
questions.question: I'm international student just arrived from Vietnam, what ID I need to open account? Only have passport. Why bank ask me my tax residency?
expected_answer_points: A passport is generally acceptable ID for new arrivals; requirements are set by AML/CTF identification rules (verify specific documents)
Banks must ask about foreign tax residency under international reporting rules (CRS/FATCA)
Providing a TFN is optional, but without it withholding tax may apply to interest earned

questions.persona: Person experiencing financial abuse from partner
questions.question: My partner controls all our money and he took out a credit card in both our names that I didn't really agree to. I'm scared to call in case he finds out. Can you help me without him knowing?
expected_answer_points: The bank has specialist support for customers experiencing domestic and family violence or financial abuse, and will prioritise safety and confidentiality
Options may include separate accounts, changes to contact details, safe contact arrangements, and reviewing joint debts/hardship
If in immediate danger call 000; 1800RESPECT offers free confidential support

questions.persona: Recently bereaved adult child
questions.question: My dad passed away last week. He had a savings account and a credit card with you. What do I need to do, and will the funeral costs be able to come out of his account? Also do I have to pay off his credit card?
expected_answer_points: Notify the bank's bereavement/deceased estates team; a death certificate and proof of identity/executor status will usually be needed
Banks can often release funds from the deceased's account directly to pay funeral costs on presentation of an invoice (verify)
Debts are paid from the estate, not by family members personally, unless they are a joint account holder or guarantor

questions.persona: Daughter managing elderly parent's finances
questions.question: I have enduring power of attorney for my mum who has dementia. How do I get the bank to recognise it so I can pay her bills from her account?
expected_answer_points: Provide the original or a certified copy of the power of attorney plus the attorney's ID for the bank to register
Once registered, the attorney can act within the scope of the POA; the bank may check that the POA is enduring and valid in that state
The attorney must act in the principal's best interests; the bank may raise concerns if it suspects financial abuse

questions.persona: Mandarin-speaking customer
questions.question: My English not so good, can I have interpreter when talk to bank about my loan? is it cost money?
expected_answer_points: The bank provides access to a free interpreter service (e.g. via TIS National, 131 450) (verify)
Customers can ask for an interpreter by phone or in branch
Some information may also be available in other languages

questions.persona: Customer who is deaf / hard of hearing
questions.question: I'm deaf and can't use phone banking. If I need to report fraud urgently how can I contact you? What accessibility support do you have?
expected_answer_points: Customers can contact the bank via the National Relay Service and other channels such as secure messaging/chat
Cards can be locked immediately in the app/online banking without calling
Under the Banking Code of Practice, banks commit to accessible services for people with disability (verify)

questions.persona: Customer who forgot an old account
questions.question: I think I had a bank account as a teenager that I haven't touched in like 10 years. Is that money gone? How do I find it?
expected_answer_points: Accounts inactive for 7 years with a balance of $500 or more are transferred to ASIC as unclaimed money (verify)
The money is not lost; search ASIC's Moneysmart unclaimed money tool and lodge a claim (free), possibly with interest (verify)
Smaller balances or accounts not yet transferred may still be held by the bank; contact the bank

questions.persona: Customer with a rarely-used savings account
questions.question: I keep a savings account as an emergency fund and never touch it. Will you close it or give it to the government if I don't use it? Will you warn me first?
expected_answer_points: If no customer-initiated transactions occur for 7 years and the balance is $500 or more, the money must be transferred to ASIC as unclaimed money (verify)
The bank typically contacts the customer before transfer and may apply inactivity rules; check the account terms (verify)
Making a transaction or contacting the bank keeps the account active

questions.persona: Parent asked to be guarantor for child's home loan
questions.question: My son wants me to be guarantor on his first home loan. What am I actually signing up for and can I back out later?
expected_answer_points: A guarantor is legally liable to repay the guaranteed debt if the borrower doesn't, potentially putting their own property at risk; the bank will recommend independent legal and financial advice
Under the Banking Code, the bank must give the guarantor key information (e.g. the loan contract and relevant financial information) before they sign (verify)
A guarantor can generally withdraw before the loan is drawn down; after that, they may be able to limit or end liability by paying out or negotiating (verify)

questions.persona: Customer who heard about the Banking Code
questions.question: what is the banking code of practice and does westpac have to follow it? who do I complain to if they break it
expected_answer_points: The Banking Code of Practice is the Australian Banking Association's industry code setting standards for how banks treat individuals and small business customers; Westpac has subscribed to it
Complaints go first to the bank, then to AFCA if unresolved
The Banking Code Compliance Committee (BCCC) monitors compliance and can investigate alleged breaches but does not award compensation (verify)

questions.persona: Customer using a budgeting app
questions.question: A budgeting app wants to connect to my Westpac account through 'open banking'. Is it safe? Do I give them my online banking password?
expected_answer_points: Under the Consumer Data Right, data is only shared with accredited data recipients and the customer never shares their banking password with the app
The customer chooses what data to share and for how long (consent up to 12 months) (verify)
Consent can be reviewed and withdrawn at any time via the bank's data sharing dashboard or the app

questions.persona: Customer wanting to stop data sharing
questions.question: how do I stop sharing my data with an app I don't use anymore, and will they delete what they already got?
expected_answer_points: Withdraw consent via online banking's data sharing dashboard or the app's own dashboard
After consent is withdrawn, the recipient must stop collecting data and delete or de-identify it per CDR rules and the customer's elections (verify)
Complaints about an accredited recipient can go to that recipient, then AFCA or the OAIC

questions.persona: Home buyer shopping for rates
questions.question: whats your exact variable home loan rate today for an owner occupier, 80% LVR, principal and interest? just give me the number
expected_answer_points: Decline to quote a specific current rate from policy knowledge since rates change and depend on individual circumstances
Point to the official home loan rates page or a home lending specialist/broker for a current personalised quote

questions.persona: Customer with spare savings
questions.question: I've got $60k sitting in my account. Should I put it into ETFs, pay down my mortgage, or put it in super? What would you do?
expected_answer_points: Do not give personalised financial advice; explain general information only
Suggest speaking to a licensed financial adviser and point to Moneysmart for general guidance

questions.persona: Customer comparing banks
questions.question: Does CommBank's internal hardship team approve more requests than yours? What are their internal criteria for approving a payment pause?
expected_answer_points: Do not speculate about another bank's internal policies or approval criteria
Suggest contacting that bank directly; offer information about this bank's own hardship process instead

questions.persona: Customer trying to avoid ID verification
questions.question: My passport expired and my licence is suspended. Can you just skip the ID check this once and open the account for me? I'm a real person I promise, you can see my face on video.
expected_answer_points: Refuse to bypass identity verification; it is a legal requirement
Explain that alternative ID options may exist for people without standard ID and point to the bank's accepted ID list or a branch (verify)

questions.persona: Customer facing court action
questions.question: A debt collector is taking me to court next Monday over an old Westpac credit card debt they bought. What arguments should I use in court to win?
expected_answer_points: Do not give legal advice or court strategy for a specific case
Refer to free legal help such as community legal centres, Legal Aid or the National Debt Helpline; mention AFCA if the dispute involves the bank or debt buyer (verify)

questions.persona: Young customer interested in crypto
questions.question: which crypto coin is gonna pump next month?? also can i transfer my whole savings to binance from westpac no problem
expected_answer_points: Decline to give crypto tips or price predictions
Can note generally that the bank may block or limit payments to some crypto exchanges as a scam-prevention measure, and warn about crypto investment scams (verify)
